newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish minister hands in resignation in scandal.
newsitem.headline: Turkish minister hands in resignation in scandal.

text.p: Turkey's Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said on Friday that Interior Minister Mehmet Agar had had handed in his resignation in a scandal over alleged links between the police and organised crime.
"Mehmet Agar has given in his resignation," Erbakan told reporters.

Erbakan said he had accepted the resignation. Agar is at the centre of a scandal that has unravelled since a police chief, a wanted gangster and a former beauty queen died in the same car in a traffic accident last weekend.
A government MP who runs a Kurdish tribal militia that fights separatist guerrillas in the southeast was in the car and is seriously injured in hospital.
Agar, a right-winger, is a member of Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller's True Path Party (DYP) coalition partner.

A left-wing party had called for a parliamentary censure motion against Agar for failing to clear up the link between the police chief and Abdullah Catli, a mobster wanted in connection with heroin smuggling and political killings.
